title: Regulatory Note — Share of Surplus Credit Paid at a Net Energy Metering Move-Out
content:
At a Net Energy Metering move-out termination, the share of the surplus that is paid depends on the rider's valuation basis and on whether the agreement's recent export credits outran the credit applied to its bills.

**Rule.** Under the legacy rider's retail energy rate basis, when the export credits banked for billing periods ended in the 12 months before the termination exceed the credit applied to bills for those periods, the surplus share is the legacy surplus share of 0.75. Under the retail-rate-less-non-bypassable-charge basis, when those export credits exceed that applied credit, it is the successor surplus share of 0.55. In every other case no reduced surplus share applies.

**Records read.** From the net metering history: the amounts of the export credits and of the credit applications whose billing periods ended in the 12 months before the termination. From the rider: its valuation basis — the retail energy rate for Rider NEM-L Legacy Net Energy Metering, the retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge for Rider NEM-R Residential Net Energy Metering and Rider NEM-A Aggregated Net Energy Metering.

## Surplus share

| Valuation basis | Export credits of the 12 months compared with credit applied for those periods | Surplus share |
|---|---|---|
| Retail energy rate | Greater | 0.75 |
| Retail energy rate less the non-bypassable charge | Greater | 0.55 |
| Either retail basis | Equal or smaller | No reduced share |
| Avoided-cost export rate | Any | No reduced share |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- Rider NEM-R agreement with export credits of 640.00 and applied credit of 590.00 for the 12 months: the exports are greater, so 0.55.
- The same agreement with exports and applied credit both 590.00: not greater, so no reduced share.
